2026 limits: 401(k)/403(b)/TSP deferral $24,500, catch-up $8,000 at 50+ (total $32,500), $11,250 at 60-63 (total $35,750); IRA $7,500 plus $1,100 at 50+; SIMPLE $17,000 plus $4,000 at 50+; 415(c) total $72,000; HCE threshold $160,000, compensation limit $360,000; HSA $4,400 self-only / $8,750 family plus $1,000 at 55+; Social Security wage base $184,500.

This is general information, not tax or financial advice. Your plan document may allow less (for example no age 60-63 catch-up). Check with your plan administrator or a tax professional.

governmental_457b.note: Separate from the 401(k)/403(b) limit, so a worker with both can defer to each. Age 50+ catch-up applies to governmental 457(b) only. The special last-3-years 457 catch-up is not covered.

simple.note: Higher SIMPLE limits apply to employers with 25 or fewer employees, or 26-100 that elect a higher contribution (SECURE 2.0 sec. 117).

ira.note: One limit shared by all traditional and Roth IRAs; capped at taxable compensation.

total_annual_additions_415c.note: Employee plus employer contributions to one employer's defined contribution plans, capped at 100% of compensation. Catch-up contributions are on top.

roth_catch_up_rule.rule: If your FICA wages (Form W-2 box 3) from the employer sponsoring the plan were over the threshold in the prior year, your age-50+ (and age 60-63) catch-up contributions to a 401(k), 403(b) or governmental 457(b) must be Roth. SIMPLE IRAs and SEPs are exempt.

Later dates apply to some governmental and collectively bargained plans.
